findings.claim: The compatibility full-read path still pre-allocates from the unverified manifest: `Vec::with_capacity(capacity)` reserves up to MAX_GRAPH_BYTES (2 GiB) based solely on `manifest.payload_bytes` before any chunk or digest verification, so a corrupt-but-schema-valid manifest can force a bounded-but-large throwaway allocation — the very trust-based allocation pattern this change eliminates elsewhere.
findings.evidence: Hunk in `read_snapshot`: `let capacity = usize::try_from(manifest.payload_bytes)...; if capacity > MAX_GRAPH_BYTES { ... } let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(capacity);` — the allocation happens before `read_snapshot_chunks_for_manifest` verifies length/digest. Contrast with the change's stated goal ('Why': 'creates an avoidable payload-sized allocation') and the new doc on `read_snapshot_chunks` ('a corrupt manifest cannot drive unbounded work').
findings.suggested_fix: Start with an empty `Vec` and let `extend_from_slice` grow it per verified-bounded chunk (or `reserve` incrementally), so allocation tracks actually stored chunk bytes rather than the manifest's unverified claim; the per-loop `total > MAX_GRAPH_BYTES` check already bounds growth.
